A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAVA and provide readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite the expanded theory, renumbering, and relocation of some content.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR10 corruption-detection and pruning experiments, Clothing1M results, and appendix experiments on incremental learning, batch size, caching, and robustness.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional comparator results and revised corruption-detection and runtime results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same within-batch and between-batch OT computations, calibrated-gradient aggregation, and label-cost caching. v2 corrects the mathematical expression for the existing Sinkhorn transport plan, but does not document a changed computational procedure or new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four CIFAR10 corruptions, CIFAR10 pruning and incremental learning, and Clothing1M valuation and pruning. The expanded appendix does not introduce another dataset, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds Data-OOB to the four CIFAR10 corruption comparisons in Figure 2. Figure 9 also adds cached Batch-wise LAVA to the runtime comparison, although Batch-wise LAVA already appeared in other experiments. The remaining comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve the corruption proportions, dataset sizes, N/4 detection and pruning protocol, feature extractors, and classifier training schedules. Revised plotted results are not accompanied by a stated protocol change. The explicit exact-OT implementation clarification is additional documentation.

E4.justification: Figure 9 revises the existing analysis of whether label-cost caching preserves detection while reducing runtime, adding cached Batch-wise LAVA as a timing comparator. The batch-size, batch-construction, incremental-learning, and Batch-wise LAVA robustness studies are retained; the relocated pruning results are not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are reported as mean plus or minus one standard deviation over five independent runs unless otherwise specified. There is no added seed policy, confidence interval, significance test, or stated increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Figures 2 and 9 substantially revise existing results as well as adding comparator curves. For example, Influence Functions' backdoor detection at approximately 1,000 examples changes from about 0.2 to about 0.6, reversing its position relative to random selection. Figure 9 revises runtime curves substantially, and cached SAVA is now described as similar in speed to LAVA rather than faster. Clothing1M's reported 70.0 ± 0.2 best accuracy and most other figures remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1's Lemma 2 relies on a reciprocal-based entropic-gradient correction. v2 introduces a revised Theorem 2 and corresponding HOT Lemma 3 using logarithmic terms and multipliers for transport-plan nonnegativity, with expanded derivations in Appendix C. It also repairs the Sinkhorn-plan expression and adds a time-complexity derivation and comparison table in Appendix D. These are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: v2 adds correcting LAVA's entropic-regularization theory and deriving the corresponding HOT trade-off as an explicit main contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. v1 primarily claims a scalable valuation method and empirical scalability. Those original claims remain, but the claimed contribution now includes a substantial theoretical correction.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly identifies dependence on a clean validation dataset as an explicit limitation. Section 2.2 also explains why scalable OT methods exploiting line, tree, or graph structures may be unsuitable for the required subgradients. Existing limitations concerning the looser validation bound and unexplored text and speech applications remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states that SAVA and LAVA use exact class-conditional OT distances rather than Gaussian approximations. It adds Data-OOB's decision-tree bagging description, default-parameter implementation reference, and a reproducibility statement. Most hardware and training details are unchanged, and the public SAVA code link already appeared in v1.

R1.justification: The relationship to LAVA changes substantially: v1 builds its theoretical argument on LAVA's theorem, whereas v2 explicitly critiques that theorem's entropy formulation and omitted constraint and claims to correct its foundation. v2 also expands coverage of scalable OT, low-rank Sinkhorn approaches, Data-OOB, and newer nearest-neighbor Shapley work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, expands explanations, adopts '(sub)gradient' terminology, updates author and publication information, and adds a reproducibility statement. The pruning discussion moves to Appendix H.1 and the theoretical appendix gains subsections, while the overall narrative and much of the existing wording remain.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference formatting, moves the notation table into the main text, adds the time-complexity table, and relocates v1 Figure 3 to appendix Figure 7. Figures 2 and 9 have expanded legends and revised plotting ranges, and Figure 1's caption is expanded. Most figure artwork is retained.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons, revised runtime evidence, complexity analysis, and implementation disclosures improve assessment of the existing scalability claim. The theoretical revision addresses defects in the earlier derivation, but its proof ends with a minus sign in Eq. (C.19) where Theorem 2 and Eq. (C.4) use a plus sign. This unresolved inconsistency limits the theoretical gain; the stronger empirical context and clearer documentation support a modest net improvement.
